THE CONTROL ROOM

Trust has a boundary.

The model cannot approve its own work. This demo gives it a declarative rule to propose, with no shell tools or production access.

01YubiKey → authorize runBound to task, model & unique run
02OpenAI → propose a ruleClaims recorded as predictions
03Host → rerun frozen checksExpected values set before the AI
04Enclave → sign releaseBound to artifact & receipt chain

Explicit fixture. No API call or hardware approval.

What the proof does — and doesn’t — establish

Reproducible: the rule’s outputs, unsupported claims, receipt integrity and signatures under the included public keys.

Requires a trust anchor: confirm key fingerprints directly with the owner. Included keys alone cannot prove who signed or that a key was hardware-backed.

Unverified: provider origin without a provider-signed attestation; complete capture of activity outside this demo; physical hardware behavior in offline fixtures.

This demonstrates blocking unsupported completion for one bounded task. It is not a general guarantee against AI fabrication or malicious code running as the same macOS account.
